translationRepairs: Gaozu, temple name the Sagely Literary, Sagely Military, Resplendent and Solemn, Filial Emperor, was of the Liu clan and originally named Zhiyuan. His forebears were Shatuo; his family later settled at Taiyuan.

Gaozu, posthumous name the Sagely Literary, Sagely Military, Resplendent and Solemn, Filial Emperor, was of the Liu clan and originally named Zhiyuan. His forebears were Shatuo; his family later settled at Taiyuan.
Focus unit opens 高祖睿文聖武昭肅孝皇帝: 高祖 is the temple name and 睿文聖武昭肅孝皇帝 the posthumous name (謚). Labeling the long honorific a “temple name” is wrong; “posthumous name” matches the Chinese.

On gengchen forebears were raised posthumously—emperors and their consorts empresses: great-grandfather Tuan received the temple name Wenzu and posthumous title Mingyuan; his consort Lady Li, Mingzhen;

On gengchen forebears were raised posthumously—emperors and their consorts empresses: great-great-grandfather Tuan received the temple name Wenzu and posthumous title Mingyuan; his consort Lady Li, Mingzhen;

Focus unit has 高祖湍 in the ancestral ladder before 曾祖昂, 祖僎, and 考典; 高祖 is the fourth-generation ancestor (great-great-grandfather). “Great-grandfather” understates the generation; the proposed label restores the correct distance.
great-great-grandfather Ang, Dezu and Gongxi; his consort Lady Yang, Gonghui;
great-grandfather Ang, Dezu and Gongxi; his consort Lady Yang, Gonghui;
Focus unit names 曾祖昂 between 高祖湍 and 祖僎; 曾祖 is great-grandfather. Calling him great-great-grandfather reverses the 高祖/曾祖 labels relative to the Chinese kinship sequence.
On bingwu the emperor set out for the Eastern Capital.
On bingshen the emperor set out for the Eastern Capital.
Focus unit dates the departure 丙申; 丙申 is bingshen, not bingwu (丙午). The replacement corrects only the sexagenary day name.
On bingwu he proceeded to the Eastern Capital.
On bingshen he proceeded to the Eastern Capital.
Literal field likewise reads 丙申 as bingwu; bingshen is the correct romanization of 丙申.
On bingwu Xue Huairang of Anguo killed the Khitan commander Liu Duo and took Xing prefecture.
On bingshen Xue Huairang of Anguo killed the Khitan commander Liu Duo and took Xing prefecture.
Focus unit opens 丙申 for Xue Huairang’s action; 丙申 is bingshen, not bingwu (丙午).
On bingwu, Anguo military commissioner Xue Huairang killed the Khitan general Liu Duo and entered Xingzhou.
On bingshen, Anguo military commissioner Xue Huairang killed the Khitan general Liu Duo and entered Xingzhou.
Literal field of the same unit misreads 丙申 as bingwu; bingshen matches the Chinese day name.
On renchen in the fourth month Guo Wei, Privy Councilor, was appointed military commissioner of Tianxiong.
On renwu in the fourth month Guo Wei, Privy Councilor, was appointed military commissioner of Tianxiong.
Focus unit dates Guo Wei’s appointment 夏四月壬午; 壬午 is renwu, not renchen (壬辰).
In the fourth month of summer, on renchen, Guo Wei the Privy Councilor was made military commissioner of Tianxiong.
In the fourth month of summer, on renwu, Guo Wei the Privy Councilor was made military commissioner of Tianxiong.
Literal field likewise has renchen for 壬午; renwu is the correct reading.
On guimao the emperor reviewed the army in the northern suburbs.
On guiwei the emperor reviewed the army in the northern suburbs.
Focus unit has 癸未 between 壬午 and 甲申; 癸未 is guiwei, not guimao (癸卯). Adjacent days confirm the consecutive sexagenary sequence.
On guimao the emperor reviewed troops at the northern suburbs.
On guiwei the emperor reviewed troops at the northern suburbs.
Literal field of the same unit misreads 癸未 as guimao; guiwei matches the Chinese and the 壬午–癸未–甲申 sequence.
Xiao Han fled to the Khitan and installed Li Congyi, Prince of Ye, to manage the Southern Court’s armies and administration.
Xiao Han fled to the Khitan and installed Li Congyi, Duke of Xun, to manage the Southern Court’s armies and administration.
Focus unit titles Li Congyi 郇國公; 郇 is Xun, not Ye (鄴), and 公 is duke. “Prince of Ye” invents the wrong fief; “Duke of Xun” restores both the place and the rank.
Xiao Han fled back to the Khitan and made Li Congyi, Prince of Ye, oversee military and state affairs of the Southern Court.
Xiao Han fled back to the Khitan and made Li Congyi, Duke of Xun, oversee military and state affairs of the Southern Court.
Literal field likewise has Prince of Ye for 郇國公; Duke of Xun matches 郇 and 公.
On jiaxu of the second month the court honored the household gate of Qu Wen of Runan in Ying prefecture for exemplary conduct.
On jiaxu of the second month the court honored the household gate of Qu Wen of Ruyin in Ying prefecture for exemplary conduct.
Focus unit places Qu Wen at 潁州汝陰; 汝陰 is Ruyin, not Runan (汝南). The replacement corrects only that place name.
On jiaxu of the second month the household gate of Qu Wen, a commoner of Runan in Ying prefecture, was marked with honor.
On jiaxu of the second month the household gate of Qu Wen, a commoner of Ruyin in Ying prefecture, was marked with honor.
Literal field of the same unit likewise has Runan for 汝陰; Ruyin is the correct reading.
In ancient usage, the first month of the year was not called “first month” either; it was called the first, or correct, month.
In ancient usage, the first month of the year was likewise not numbered as “one”; it was called the Correct Month.
Focus unit says 亦不云一，而曰正月: ancients avoided the numeral “one” and used 正月. The before text wrongly denies then reaffirms “first month”; the proposed wording restores 不云一 and Correct Month for 正月.
The Discourses of the States, speaking of the six pitch-pipes, says yuan comes between and dalu; the Zhouyi, listing the six lines, says initial nine.
The Discourses of the States, speaking of the six pitch-pipes, says yuanjian Dalü; the Zhouyi, listing the six lines, says initial nine.

Focus unit cites 元間大呂 as Guoyu wording that uses 元 (for the first of the six 間) with 大呂; reading 間 as the verb “comes between” is wrong. The proposal’s “Yuanjian and Dalu” wrongly splits the phrase into two pitch names; keep it as one cited phrase yuanjian Dalü parallel to 初九.
